body_en: UK court orders Global Airlines into liquidation - Aviation24.be

The UK’s Insolvency and Companies Court ordered the compulsory liquidation of Global Airlines Ltd on 4 November 2026, following a creditor petition filed in May. The winding-up notice was published in The Gazette on 12 November.

Founded by James Asquith in 2021, the British start-up planned to build a transatlantic network around the Airbus A380. It never obtained its own air operator certificate. Its only passenger services were a series of charter flights linking Glasgow and Manchester with New York in May 2025, operated by Hi Fly Malta under the Global Airlines brand.
The venture’s sole A380, 9H-GLOBL , has been in storage at Tarbes in south-west France since July 2025. Its fate remains unclear.
Companies House also records a separate application to strike Global Airlines Aircraft Ltd off the register. The court’s winding-up order concerns Global Airlines Ltd .

body_en: British Airways A321neo goes around after Heathrow tailstrike - Aviation24.be
Home Airports Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (AMS) British Airways A321neo goes around after Heathrow tailstrike

British Airways flight BA431 from Amsterdam Schiphol went around after a tailstrike during landing at London Heathrow on 12 November 2026. The Airbus A321neo, registered G-TNEB, landed safely on its second approach about 14 minutes later. No injuries were reported.

The incident occurred at about 10:35 local time on runway 27L. Footage from two airport cameras appears to show the aircraft bouncing on touchdown and its tail contacting the runway twice before the crew climbed away. The Aviation Safety Network recorded a tailstrike during touchdown and listed the extent of the damage as unknown.
British Airways took the aircraft out of service for inspection and said it was assisting the UK Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) with its investigation.

The cause of the bounced landing remains undetermined. Heathrow’s 10:20 weather observation, about 15 minutes before the incident, recorded light rain, an overcast cloud base at 1,400 feet and a south-southeasterly wind at 11 knots.

2026 年 11 月 12 日，从阿姆斯特丹史基浦起飞的英国航空 BA431 航班在伦敦希思罗机场着陆时尾部撞击后复飞。这架注册为 G-TNEB 的空客 A321neo 大约 14 分钟后在第二次进场时安全着陆。没有人员受伤的报告。
事件发生在当地时间上午10时35分左右，地点为27L跑道。两个机场摄像机的镜头似乎显示，飞机在接地时弹起，机尾两次接触跑道，然后机组人员爬离。航空安全网络记录了着陆期间发生的尾部撞击事件，并将损坏程度列为未知。
英国航空公司已将这架飞机停飞接受检查，并表示正在协助英国航空事故调查处（AAIB）进行调查。
弹跳着陆的原因尚未确定。事发前约 15 分钟，希思罗机场 10 点 20 分的天气观测记录到有小雨，云底高度为 1,400 英尺阴，风速为 11 节/小时。

A Turkish military Sikorsky S-70 helicopter crashed on the southern outskirts of Malatya on Thursday evening, 12 November, killing four military personnel on board, the Turkish Defence Ministry said.

The helicopter came down near a cluster of buildings in the Samanköy neighbourhood. Police, firefighters and medical teams were sent to the scene. The Demirören News Agency reported that fire from the wreckage spread to a nearby house, with no casualties reported on the ground.
The Defence Ministry said the cause of the crash had yet to be determined.

body_en: IATA warns only half of air accident probes yield public final reports - Aviation24.be
Home Miscellaneous Accidents IATA warns only half of air accident probes yield public final reports
IATA - International Air Transport Association

Only about half of aviation accidents investigated under international rules result in a published final report, according to Mark Searle, IATA’s global director of safety. Speaking to Reuters at the International Aviation Safety Summit in Montreal on 12 November, Searle said publication rates had shown little improvement, limiting the industry’s ability to learn from accidents and act on safety recommendations.

Under ICAO’s Annex 13 framework, investigators should publish a final report as soon as possible and, if possible, within 12 months. If the report is still pending, the investigating authority should publish an interim statement on each anniversary of the accident, outlining progress and any safety issues identified. The purpose of the investigation is to prevent future accidents.

A joint industry paper published in February 2025 gives a historical benchmark. IATA data showed that investigations had been completed for 140 of the 268 accidents recorded from 2018 to 2023, or 52%, as of 30 June 2024. Hassan Shahidi, president of the Flight Safety Foundation, told Reuters that investigating agencies often cite shortages of suitably qualified staff.

Reuters cited two high-profile cases still awaiting final reports as of 12 November: the June 2025 crash of an Air India Boeing 787 shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad, which killed 260 people, and the 2022 China Eastern Airlines crash.

首页 其他事故 国际航空运输协会警告说，只有一半的航空事故调查得出公开的最终报告
IATA-国际航空运输协会
国际航空运输协会全球安全总监马克·塞尔表示，根据国际规则调查的航空事故中，只有大约一半会发布最终报告。 11 月 12 日，塞尔在蒙特利尔举行的国际航空安全峰会上向路透社表示，发表率几乎没有改善，限制了该行业从事故中吸取教训并根据安全建议采取行动的能力。
根据国际民航组织附件 13 框架，调查人员应尽快发布最终报告，如有可能，应在 12 个月内发布。如果报告仍在等待中，调查当局应在事故周年纪念日发布一份临时声明，概述进展情况和发现的任何安全问题。调查的目的是为了防止未来发生事故。
2025 年 2 月发表的一份行业联合论文给出了历史基准。国际航空运输协会的数据显示，截至 2024 年 6 月 30 日，2018 年至 2023 年记录的 268 起事故中，有 140 起事故的调查已完成，即 52%。飞行安全基金会主席哈桑·沙希迪 (Hassan Shahidi) 告诉路透社，调查机构经常指出缺乏合格的工作人员。
路透社援引了截至 11 月 12 日仍在等待最终报告的两起备受瞩目的案件：2025 年 6 月印度航空一架波音 787 从艾哈迈达巴德起飞后不久坠毁，造成 260 人死亡，以及 2022 年中国东方航空坠机事故。

His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America.

Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand.

Alaska Airlines ' largest hub, Seattle (SEA), is about to gain four new nonstop domestic flights, as the airline adds services to Charlotte, Des Moines, Jacksonville and Norfolk. These routes will all operate daily.

According to aviation blogger Enilria , the one world carrier will expand its domestic reach from Washington State, following the airline's announcement of plans to operate flights to Guadalajara in Mexico and nonstop services from Anchorage to Tokyo .

Beginning on June 10, 2027, Alaska will take on American Airlines , with both carriers connecting the East to the West. This will be Alaska's only service to Charlotte, where it will go head-to-head with American, which holds more than 89% market share at the airport.

Flights from Seattle will depart for Charlotte in the morning for a late-afternoon arrival, while return flights leave in the early evening for a late-night arrival back in Seattle. The route will be served year-round.
Alaska will fly its Boeing 737-900ER on the service to Charlotte, whereas American typically operates the Airbus A321 on its service to Seattle. Below is Alaska's schedule to Charlotte

On the same day that Alaska debuts its new service to Charlotte, the airline will also begin its year-round service to Norfolk International Airport (ORF). Alaska will become the only airline serving the route, with the service expected to operate daily. Flights will depart from Seattle at 7:30 AM each morning, with return flights departing at 5:01 PM. Flights will be operated by the airline's Boeing 737 aircraft.

Jacksonville will also be on the airline's menu, as the airline plans to introduce nonstop flights from June 24. The route will become the airline's longest domestic service, covering 2,439 miles (3,924 kilometers). Service will take five and a half hours from Seattle.
These will be brand new routes from Seattle, with no other airline having operated them previously.

title_en: Is It True That The Airbus A321XLR Flies With Its Nose Pitched Up At Cruising Altitude?
title_zh: 空客 A321XLR 在巡航高度飞行时机头上翘是真的吗？
summary: Why the longest range single-aisle in the Airbus line up is always pointed skyward.
summary_zh: 为什么空客系列中航程最长的单通道飞机总是指向天空。
body_en: Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

Did you feel like your plane was a little nose-up on your last long flight? Well, you're not wrong. In fact, nearly every single commercial jetliner cruises with a noticeable nose-high pitch for most of the journey. The physics of flight dictate that an aircraft on a steady level cruise rarely maintains a perfectly parallel relationship with the horizon. It's especially remarkable on Airbus ' newest long-haul narrowbody, the A321XLR.

While a nose-up attitude is basic physics, a couple of factors make it highly noticeable on the A321XLR. An aircraft wing does not generate lift when aligned perfectly flat with the oncoming air mass. It requires a pitch of two to three degrees above the horizon to force the air under the wings and produce efficient lift. The A321 is a very long narrowbody aircraft, and its silhouette creates a clear visual profile compared to shorter aircraft like the A319.

This is not an abnormality of the A321XLR design. It is the standard operating condition for the entire commercial fleet, ranging from the small Airbus A220 to the massive Boeing 777 . As a flight progresses and the engines burn through fuel, the plane becomes lighter. When it needs less lift, the fly-by-wire system gradually lowers the nose. The cabin floor is rarely level, though the tilt is subtle enough that most passengers won't notice it while seated.
The Mechanics Of Cruise Pitch: Weight And Flight Dynamics

Despite carrying far more weight than other planes in its class, the XLR retains the Airbus A321's baseline wingspan of 117 feet (35.8 meters). Given the restricted wing area compared to a widebody jet that flies similar routes as the XLR, it must fly at a higher angle of attack than many commercial jets. Raising the nose one to two degrees above most other airliners allows the XLR to generate more lift at a similar altitude and airspeed.

It must take off with a far greater payload than the standard A321neo , which is often configured with a higher seating capacity, because of the fuel it carries to make long journeys. That requires gradual step climbs with the XLR slowly raising and lowering its altitude relative to the fuel in its tanks as the route progresses.

Pilots on simulator forums online cite pitch ranges between one and three degrees for cruise flight. These values fluctuate depending on the precise fuel load, passenger count, and chosen speed schedule. Weight is the primary driver of these fluctuations. For the Airbus A321XLR, this calculation is pushed to the absolute extreme of the single-aisle category. The jet stands out as the heaviest iteration of the A321 family, boasting a maximum takeoff weight reaching 223,000 pounds (101,100 kg).

When heavily loaded with fuel at takeoff, the thin air at high altitudes cannot provide enough density to support an XLR efficiently. To avoid an unfavorable flight profile, the XLR is heavily reliant on step climbs. It will initially level off at a lower altitude where the air is denser. Even at this lower altitude, the engines must operate at high thrust to maintain cruise speed while holding a high nose pitch.
Nose-Up Cruising: Passenger Perception and Safety Envelopes

Walking toward the front of the A321XLR cabin on a transatlantic flight might make a passenger feel as though they are moving up a shallow ramp. While the plane behaves flawlessly from an engineering standpoint, its high nose-up posture changes how passengers experience the flight. That is most noticeable during the initial hours of a transcontinental mission when the aircraft is heaviest.

In the early phase of such a trip, flight attendants must manage heavy galley carts on a tilted floor. Service typically starts from the front of the cabin and moves backward, allowing the crew to push the heavy carts downhill rather than fighting gravity to push them forward. To guarantee a pleasant ride for a full passenger payload, the aircraft relies on a highly optimized, non-emergency 'comfort envelope.'

To prevent passengers from feeling any sudden jerks or wallowing motions, the autopilot performs continuous micro-trimming. The computers maintain a specific cruise speed, typically Mach 0.78, at an altitude where the air density allows the plane to ride smoothly. By keeping the XLR in the 'buffet margin' performance band, the system ensures a rock-solid, vibration-free ride for the customers in the back.
Engineering Solutions And Automation At Airbus

Inside the advanced cockpit of the A321XLR, a suite of flight computers handles most of the workload required to balance the jet's pitch. The flight computers eliminate the need for pilots to manually adjust the plane's controls as the trip progresses. These avionics let the flight crew spend more time focused on navigation rather than constantly correcting the aircraft's attitude.

Flying at a nose-up angle naturally creates extra aerodynamic drag. To combat this, the computer systems linking the navigation data and the engine throttles work together seamlessly. The autopilot uses a continuous feedback loop that monitors how the aircraft is interacting with the thin air. As the plane burns off fuel and changes mass, the computer automatically commands the tail stabilizers to pivot by microdegrees.

This smooth, automated adjustment gently lowers the nose to a flatter angle without requiring any input from the flight crew. The system calculates the exact engine thrust needed to glide efficiently at the ideal angle. It maintains a steady cruise speed without burning excess fuel, keeping the plane at the mathematically perfect intersection of pitch, speed, and fuel efficiency.
Calculating Step Climbs And High-Altitude Safety Guards

The A321XLR navigation computer removes all the guesswork from changing altitudes during long-haul flights. The plane cannot safely cruise at its final high altitude right after takeoff because the air is too thin to support it. The automation constantly runs real-time calculations to find the optimal moments to climb. Simultaneously, flying a long-range narrowbody like the XLR near its performance margins also requires strict safety boundaries.

When the plane reaches an ideal state, the system notifies the crew, executes the climb smoothly, and automatically recalibrates the nose position for the new altitude. The flight control software also includes hard-coded safety protections that act as an invisible safety net. If severe turbulence or a sudden wind shift tries to force the nose into a dangerously high angle, the computer automatically intervenes. It overrides unsafe tendencies and stabilizes the plane well before it approaches an aerodynamic stall.
body_zh: 卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
在上次长途飞行中，您是否感觉您的飞机有点倾斜？嗯，你没有错。事实上，几乎每架商用喷气式客机在大部分旅程中都会以明显的机头高度进行巡航。飞行的物理原理决定了稳定水平巡航的飞机很少与地平线保持完全平行的关系。这在空客最新的长途窄体飞机 A321XLR 上尤其引人注目。
虽然机头向上的姿态是基本物理原理，但有几个因素使其在 A321XLR 上非常引人注目。当飞机机翼与迎面而来的气团完全平坦时，不会产生升力。它需要距地平线两到三度的俯仰角，以迫使机翼下方的空气产生有效的升力。 A321 是一款非常长的窄体飞机，与 A319 等较短的飞机相比，其轮廓营造出清晰的视觉轮廓。
这并不是 A321XLR 设计的异常。这是整个商业机队的标准运行条件，从小型空客 A220 到大型波音 777。随着飞行的进行和发动机燃烧燃料，飞机变得更轻。当需要较小的升力时，电传操纵系统会逐渐降低机头。机舱地板很少是水平的，尽管倾斜程度足够微妙，大多数乘客在坐下时不会注意到它。
巡航变桨的力学：重量和飞行动力学
尽管 XLR 的重量远高于其他同类飞机，但仍保留了空客 A321 117 英尺（35.8 米）的基线翼展。考虑到与 XLR 类似航线的宽体喷气式飞机相比，机翼面积有限，因此它必须以比许多商用喷气式飞机更高的迎角飞行。将机头比大多数其他客机抬高一到两度，使 XLR 能够在相似的高度和空速下产生更大的升力。
它必须以比标准 A321neo 大得多的有效载荷起飞，而标准 A321neo 通常配置有更高的座位容量，因为它携带用于长途旅行的燃料。这需要逐步爬升，随着路线的进展，XLR 相对于油箱中的燃料缓慢升高和降低其高度。
在线模拟器论坛上的飞行员引用巡航飞行的俯仰范围为一到三度。这些值会根据精确的燃油负载、乘客数量和所选的速度表而波动。体重是这些波动的主要驱动因素。对于空客 A321XLR，这种计算被推向了单通道类别的绝对极限。该喷气式飞机是 A321 系列中最重的机型，最大起飞重量达到 223,000 磅（101,100 公斤）。
当起飞时大量装载燃油时，高空稀薄的空气无法提供足够的密度来有效支持 XLR。为了避免不利的飞行剖面，XLR 严重依赖阶梯爬升。最初它将在空气密度较低的较低高度趋于平稳。即使在如此低的高度，发动机也必须以高推力运行，以在保持高机头俯仰的同时保持巡航速度。
抬头巡航：乘客感知和安全范围
在跨大西洋航班上，走向 A321XLR 机舱的前部可能会让乘客感觉自己好像正在走上一个浅坡道。虽然从工程角度来看，这架飞机的表现完美无缺，但其高机头向上的姿势改变了乘客的飞行体验。这在跨大陆任务的最初几个小时内最为明显，此时飞机最重。
在此类旅行的早期阶段，空乘人员必须在倾斜的地板上管理重型厨房推车。服务通常从机舱前部开始向后移动，使工作人员能够将重型推车推下山，而不是对抗重力将它们向前推。为了保证满载乘客的愉快飞行，飞机依赖于高度优化的非紧急“舒适包络”。
为了防止乘客感到突然的抽搐或摇摆运动，自动驾驶仪会进行连续的微调。计算机在空气密度允许飞机平稳飞行的高度保持特定的巡航速度，通常为 0.78 马赫。通过将 XLR 保持在“自助裕度”性能范围内，该系统可确保后排乘客获得坚如磐石、无振动的乘坐体验。
空中客车公司的工程解决方案和自动化
在 A321XLR 的先进驾驶舱内，一套飞行计算机处理平衡飞机俯仰所需的大部分工作负载。飞行计算机使飞行员无需在飞行过程中手动调整飞机的控制装置。这些航空电子设备让机组人员可以将更多时间集中在导航上，而不是不断纠正飞机的姿态。
以机头向上的角度飞行自然会产生额外的空气动力阻力。为了解决这个问题，连接导航数据和发动机油门的计算机系统无缝地协同工作。自动驾驶仪使用连续反馈回路来监控飞机如何与稀薄的空气相互作用。当飞机燃烧掉燃料并改变质量时，计算机会自动命令尾部稳定器以微度旋转。
这种平稳、自动的调整可以轻轻地将机头降低到更平坦的角度，而不需要机组人员的任何输入。该系统计算以理想角度有效滑行所需的精确发动机推力。它可以保持稳定的巡航速度，而不会燃烧多余的燃油，从而使飞机在俯仰、速度和燃油效率方面保持数学上的完美交集。
计算阶梯攀爬和高空安全防护装置
A321XLR 导航计算机消除了长途飞行期间高度变化的所有猜测。由于空气太稀薄，无法支撑飞机，因此飞机在起飞后无法在最终高空安全巡航。自动化系统不断运行实时计算，以找到最佳的攀爬时刻。同时，在接近其性能裕度的情况下飞行像 XLR 这样的远程窄体飞机也需要严格的安全界限。
当飞机达到理想状态时，系统通知机组人员，平稳执行爬升，并自动重新校准机头位置以适应新的高度。飞行控制软件还包括硬编码的安全保护措施，充当隐形的安全网。如果严重的湍流或突然的风向试图迫使机头进入危险的高角度，计算机会自动干预。它克服了不安全的倾向，并在飞机接近空气动力失速之前稳定飞机。

title_en: FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop, Shuts Down The Skies: What’s Going On?
title_zh: 美国联邦航空局（FAA）在全国范围内发布地面停止令，关闭天空：发生了什么事？
summary: The FAA has issued a nationwide ground stop "due to extraordinary circumstances," halting departures across the US. Here's what we know so far about the possible causes.
summary_zh: “由于特殊情况”，美国联邦航空局已在全国范围内停止起飞，停止了美国各地的航班起飞。以下是我们目前所知道的有关 t 的信息
body_en: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a nationwide ground stop, which is pretty unprecedented. Admittedly we’ve had our fair share of air traffic control issues in the United States over the years. But this is really on a different level, unlike anything we’ve seen since 9/11, in terms of operational disruptions. I guess it’s fitting that this is happening on Friday the 13th.
Flights grounded “due to extraordinary circumstances”
At 3:54PM ET today (Friday, November 13, 2026), the FAA issued a ground stop for flights across the country, as pilots received the following message

DUE TO EXTRAORDINARY CIRCUMSTANCES AND FOR REASONS OF SAFETY. ATTENTION ALL AIRCRAFT OPERATORS, BY ORDER OF THE FEDERAL AVIATION COMMAND CENTER ALL AIRPORTS ARE GROUND STOPPED. ALL DEPARTING TRAFFIC SHOULD REMAIN GROUND STOPPED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. INBOUND INTERNATIONAL FLIGHTS WILL BE MANAGED ON A CASE BY CASE BASIS.

As of now, the ground stop is through 11:30PM ET, though it’s possible that it’s lifted before then. That timeline clearly reflects the extent to which the current situation is a complete mess, and this won’t be an easy fix.

As usual, JonNYC was among the first to break the news, and he even reported on this before the official ground stop was issued, when airports in the Northeast started having issues, prior to this going nationwide.

Boston Center, New York Center, Chicago Center, New York Approach have all lost numerous frequencies. All facilities are in ATC Alert. Some sectors in New York Center are unable any traffic currently. Numerous— I mean NUMEROUS frequencies…

“All airspace is currently being sterilized and centers are preparing for ATC Zero operations. Airborne’s should NOT be majorly effected— i.e, at least for now, this is not a “9/11 type of event” where airbornes are being forced to land at the closest airport available. All…

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed this development a while later, sharing that there were “communication issues impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” and he stated that “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”

The @FAAnews issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them.
Secretary Sean Duffy (@SecDuffy) November 13, 2026
As of now, there’s no timeline for this ground stop ending. To my knowledge, I believe this is now the most significant ground stop we’ve seen in the United States in over 25 years (since 9/11).

If you’re flying this weekend, expect that things will be a mess. To those flying right now, good luck. Ford is on a flight that was supposed to depart at 3:59PM, so suffice it to say that he had some pretty bad luck here, as they pushed back, and then this happened. I hope not too many others are in the same situation.

There’s a major issue when you have flights landing but flights can’t depart, since you have way more planes than gates. So get ready to be patient if you’re onboard a flight, given the complicated logistics.
Is this a tech glitch, a cyber attack, or what’s going on?
What could explain an air traffic outage of this scale? As of now, all we can do is speculate, though there are a few interesting things to point out.

First, it remains to be seen if this is related, but the FAA reportedly began its rollout of the new AI-powered air traffic management tool this week, known as SMART (which stands for “Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories”).

Timing-wise, it seems like there’s a possibility this could be related. At the same time, you wouldn’t assume this leads to communication issues, which is what seems to be going on here. So it’s worth pointing out the timing, but we have no reason to believe the two things are related.

Yes the FAA began its nationwide rollout of the SMART AI for ARTCCs to use this week. It’s not clear at this time if the rollout is related to this outage, but if it’s a rolling communications issue, it’s much more likely it’s within already established equipment pilots-ATC use https://t.co/PXqSFdOA1q
Oriana Pawlyk (@Oriana0214) November 13, 2026
body_zh: 美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）已发布全国范围内的地面停飞令，这是史无前例的。诚然，多年来我们在美国也遇到过相当多的空中交通管制问题。但就运营中断而言，这确实是一个不同的层面，与 9/11 以来我们所看到的任何情况都不同。我想这发生在 13 号星期五是很合适的。
“由于特殊情况”航班停飞
美国东部时间今天下午 3:54（2026 年 11 月 13 日星期五），美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 对全国各地的航班发出地面停止通知，飞行员收到以下消息
由于特殊情况和安全原因。所有飞机运营商请注意，根据联邦航空指挥中心的命令，所有机场均已停飞。所有出发交通均应保持地面停止状态，直至另行通知。入境国际航班将根据具体情况进行管理。
截至目前，地面停止时间为东部时间晚上 11:30，不过有可能在此之前解除。该时间表清楚地反映了当前局势的混乱程度，而这并不是一个容易解决的问题。
和往常一样，JonNYC 是最先爆料这一消息的人之一，他甚至在官方地面停止发布之前就报道了这一消息，当时东北部的机场开始出现问题，然后再扩展到全国。
波士顿中心、纽约中心、芝加哥中心、纽约方法都失去了许多频率。所有设施均处于 ATC 警报状态。纽约中心的部分路段目前无法通行。无数——我的意思是无数频率……
“所有空域目前正在消毒，各中心正在为空管零号行动做准备。空降兵不应受到重大影响——也就是说，至少目前，这不是“9/11 类型的事件”，空降兵被迫降落在最近的机场。所有……
运输部长肖恩·达菲（Sean Duffy）稍后证实了这一进展，并表示“存在影响所有航线交通控制中心的通信问题”，并表示“美国联邦航空局的技术人员正在调查该问题”。
在影响所有航线交通控制中心的通信问题后，@FAAnews 向所有美国机场发出了全国范围内的地面停车通知。美国联邦航空局的技术人员正在调查这个问题。我们将立即提供最新消息。
国务卿肖恩·达菲 (@SecDuffy) 2026 年 11 月 13 日
截至目前，尚无此次地面停留结束的时间表。据我所知，我相信这是 25 年来（自 9/11 事件以来）我们在美国看到的最重要的地面停留。
如果你这个周末要坐飞机，预计事情会变得一团糟。对于那些正在飞行的人来说，祝你好运。福特乘坐的航班原定于下午 3:59 起飞，所以可以说他在这里运气不太好，因为他们推迟了，然后就发生了这种情况。我希望不要有太多其他人处于同样的情况。
当航班降落但航班无法起飞时，就会出现一个重大问题，因为飞机数量远多于登机口数量。因此，考虑到复杂的后勤工作，如果您乘坐航班，请做好耐心等待。
这是技术故障、网络攻击还是发生了什么？
如何解释如此规模的空中交通中断？截至目前，我们所能做的就是猜测，尽管有一些有趣的事情需要指出。
首先，这是否相关还有待观察，但据报道，美国联邦航空局本周开始推出新的人工智能空中交通管理工具，称为 SMART（代表“空域、航线和轨迹的战略管理”）。
从时间上来看，这似乎有可能是相关的。同时，您不会认为这会导致沟通问题，而这似乎就是这里发生的情况。因此值得指出时间，但我们没有理由相信这两件事是相关的。
是的，美国联邦航空局本周开始在全国范围内推出供 ARTCC 使用的 SMART AI。目前尚不清楚此次推出是否与此次中断有关，但如果是滚动通信问题，则更有可能是在已经建立的设备试点中 - ATC 使用 https://t.co/PXqSFdOA1q

title_en: Delta Air Lines Is Already Flying The Replacement For Its Aging Airbus A319s, But American & United Don't Have One
title_zh: 达美航空已开始为其老化的空客 A319 更换飞机，但美国航空和联合航空还没有飞机
summary: A closer look at why American and United don't want a straight replacement for their A319s.
summary_zh: 仔细看看为什么美国航空和联合航空不想直接更换他们的 A319 飞机。
body_en: Daniel comes to Simple Flying with a business focused approach to the aviation world. Daniel enjoys analyzing strategy and how companies move against each other to gain a step ahead in the skies. Besides strategy, Daniel also has a passion for aircraft design and the history of aviation.

American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and United Airlines all operate the Airbus A319 . Together, the three operate over 250 examples, using it as a core aircraft slotting above their regional jets and underneath their larger narrowbodies. However, the aircraft is also old, having debuted in 1996.

The US carriers need to replace these aircraft soon, yet two out of the three haven't ordered the Airbus A319neo, Boeing 737 MAX 7, Airbus A220, or Embraer E2. Delta Air Lines has ordered 145 Airbus A220s, split between 45 A220-100s and 100 A220-300s. The 109-seat A220-100s are much smaller than an A319-100 and are really sized closer to the airline's Boeing 717-200s.

The 130-seat A220-300s, however, are almost perfectly sized to replace the 132-seat A319-100s. The other airlines have not ordered this aircraft, nor any others to replace their A319s (as well as the 737-700 in the case of United). However, they might not need these planes to replace the A319-100.
Delta's A220 Fleet & The Circumstances Of The Order

Delta first ordered the A220 back in 2016 when the aircraft was still being sold by Bombardier as the CSeries. At the time, the CSeries was a promising plane, but orders were relatively scarce, and Bombardier was desperate to break into the US market in particular. The original order consisted of 75 CS100s (now the A220-100), and Delta received the planes at such an attractive price that it prompted Boeing to file an anti-dumping petition, which was later overturned.

Delta got an amazing price for these planes that is unlikely to be matched. The aircraft is, of course, excellent for its intended missions, but capital cost plays a huge part in the economics of acquiring and operating an aircraft type. The circumstances of the order make the A220 more compelling for Delta than it would be if American or United ordered the type simply because they would need to pay more money.

This is especially true when considering that it would come with high integration costs. Delta has experienced excellent results with the A220, and has since added 70 orders in total . While the original order solely consisted of 75 CS100s/A220-100s, all subsequent orders have been for the A319-sized A220-300.

Meanwhile, the airline has converted 30 A220-100 orders to the larger variant. While the A220-100 is a competent aircraft in its own right, the A220-300 has more seats without burning significantly more fuel, and the aircraft doesn't even have a significant range penalty for most airlines' purposes.

While the US airlines operate large fleets of last-generation small widebodies, American and United have not ordered any current-generation examples. However, this is because their replacement for the A319-100 is the A321neo and the 737 MAX 10. Both airlines have been upgauging because the A321neo and 737 MAX 10 offer significantly better per-seat economics than other narrowbody aircraft.

This makes them much more compelling to operate than their smaller counterparts. American Airlines has ordered 206 A321neos in total while also acquiring ten used examples, and it's ordered 115 737 MAX 10s. United Airlines has ordered 210 A321neos, 224 737 MAX 9s, and 167 737 MAX 10s. Both airlines have also ordered the 737 MAX 8, but in smaller numbers (103 for American and 123 for United).

What will actually happen is the new large narrowbodies will take over the carrier's highest demand routes, displacing smaller aircraft down the network and sending the A319-100s to the scrapyard. Delta has done this exact thing, ordering 100 737 MAX 10s and 189 A321neos. While it is taking new A220s, these aircraft are not necessarily replacing the A319-100s one for one.

Instead, Delta will again use its new large narrowbodies to take over its busiest routes, which will displace other aircraft, including the A220s in some cases. Meanwhile, the A319-100s will go away. For all three airlines, it's their large narrowbodies that will enable displacements throughout the network.

Over the past 15 years, Delta has ordered 145 A220s, while it also leased 88 717s from Southwest Airlines for an exceptionally low price . American Airlines ordered 32 A319-100s new from Airbus. Otherwise, all of Delta's narrowbody orders have been for the A321-200, A321neo, 737-900ER, and 737 MAX 10. American has otherwise only ordered the A321-200, A321neo, 737-800, 737 MAX 8, and 737 MAX 10.

Similarly, United has only taken the A321neo, 737-800, 737-900ER, 737 MAX 8, and 737 MAX 9, while holding orders for the MAX 10. There has been a noticeable trend of US airlines favoring larger narrowbodies, and even the mid-size 737-800s and 737 MAX 8s have fallen out of favor.

These aircraft simply deliver superior economics to the shrinks in their families, as the added fuel burn is far outweighed by their increased revenue potential. The tradeoff is shorter range and runway performance, but only a handful of mainline stations have truly challenging conditions. At the same time, the A320neo and 737 MAX families have solved the performance and range issues.

Across the board, US airlines are upgauging, switching to larger aircraft for short-haul flights. In the past, another reason why airlines would buy smaller aircraft is to right-size capacity, but the US legacy carriers have strongly employed fare segmentation as a core commercial strategy.

This has reduced the need to operate smaller narrowbodies, since releasing various numbers of differently priced tickets can help fill planes on slower days. This is something that United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby has publicly commented on.

Fare segmentation and basic economy fares mean that his airline no longer requires a small narrowbody to meet demand, allowing United to standardize on larger, more economical aircraft. Tellingly, United ordered 45 737-700s in 2016, added another 20 units, then converted all orders to the 737-800 and 737 MAX 9 later the same year .

American Airlines ordered 32 A319-100s new from Airbus, while also acquiring a handful of used examples. United Airlines converted all of its later 737-700 orders to larger variants, while also acquiring a handful of used A319-100s. Delta, on the other hand, ordered 145 A220s while also acquiring 88 717s. Of course, the capital costs play a huge role in this.
body_zh: Daniel 带着以商业为中心的方式进入航空界，加入了 Simple Flying。丹尼尔喜欢分析战略以及公司如何相互竞争以取得领先一步。除了战略之外，丹尼尔还对飞机设计和航空历史充满热情。
美国航空、达美航空和联合航空均运营空客 A319 飞机。这三家公司总共运营了 250 多架飞机，将其用作核心飞机，安装在支线喷气式飞机上方和大型窄体飞机下方。然而，这架飞机也很老旧，于 1996 年首次亮相。
美国航空公司需要尽快更换这些飞机，但三分之二尚未订购空客 A319neo、波音 737 MAX 7、空客 A220 或巴西航空工业公司 E2。达美航空已订购 145 架空客 A220，其中包括 45 架 A220-100 和 100 架 A220-300。 109 座的 A220-100 比 A319-100 小得多，而且尺寸实际上更接近该航空公司的波音 717-200。
然而，130 座的 A220-300 的尺寸几乎可以完美取代 132 座的 A319-100。其他航空公司尚未订购这架飞机，也没有订购任何其他飞机来替换其 A319 飞机（以及联合航空的 737-700）。然而，他们可能不需要这些飞机来取代 A319-100。
达美航空 A220 机队及订单情况
达美航空于 2016 年首次订购 A220，当时庞巴迪仍在以 C 系列的名义销售该飞机。当时，C系列是一款很有前途的飞机，但订单相对稀缺，庞巴迪尤其迫切希望打入美国市场。最初的订单包括 75 架 CS100（现在的 A220-100），达美航空以极具吸引力的价格接收了这些飞机，以至于促使波音公司提出反倾销请愿书，但后来被推翻。
达美航空为这些飞机提供了令人难以置信的惊人价格。当然，该飞机非常适合其预定任务，但资本成本在购买和运营飞机类型的经济性中起着重要作用。与美国航空或联合航空仅仅因为需要支付更多费用而订购该机型相比，该订单的情况使 A220 对达美航空更具吸引力。
考虑到它会带来高昂的集成成本，这一点尤其正确。达美航空 A220 取得了优异的成绩，自此以来总共增加了 70 架订单。虽然最初的订单仅包括 75 架 CS100/A220-100，但随后的所有订单都是 A319 尺寸的 A220-300。
与此同时，该航空公司已将 30 架 A220-100 订单改装为更大的型号。虽然 A220-100 本身就是一款称职的飞机，但 A220-300 拥有更多座位，且不会消耗更多燃油，而且对于大多数航空公司而言，该飞机甚至没有明显的航程损失。
虽然美国航空公司运营着由最新一代小型宽体飞机组成的大型机队，但美国航空和联合航空尚未订购任何当前一代的飞机。然而，这是因为 A319-100 的替代品是 A321neo 和 737 MAX 10。两家航空公司一直在升级，因为 A321neo 和 737 MAX 10 提供比其他窄体飞机更好的每座经济性。
这使得它们比规模较小的同行更具吸引力。美国航空总共订购了 206 架 A321neo，同时还购买了 10 架二手飞机，其中订购了 115 737 MAX 10。美国联合航空已订购 210 架 A321neo、224 737 MAX 9 和 167 737 MAX 10。两家航空公司还订购了 737 MAX 8，但数量较少（美国航空 103 架，联合航空 123 架）。
实际发生的情况是，新型大型窄体飞机将接管该航空公司需求最高的航线，取代网络中的小型飞机，并将 A319-100 送往废品场。达美航空已经做到了这一点，订购了 100 737 MAX 10 和 189 架 A321neo。虽然它正在使用新的 A220 飞机，但这些飞机不一定会一一取代 A319-100 飞机。
相反，达美航空将再次使用其新型大型窄体飞机来接管其最繁忙的航线，这将取代其他飞机，包括在某些情况下的 A220 飞机。与此同时，A319-100 将消失。对于这三家航空公司来说，大型窄体飞机将在整个网络中实现位移。

在过去的15年里，达美航空已经订购了145架A220飞机，同时还以极低的价格从西南航空租赁了88 717飞机。美国航空从空中客车公司订购了 32 架新的 A319-100 飞机。除此之外，达美航空的所有窄体机订单都是 A321-200、A321neo、737-900ER 和 737 MAX 10。美国航空仅订购了 A321-200、A321neo、737-800、737 MAX 8 和 737 MAX 10。
同样，美联航只接收了A321neo、737-800、737-900ER、737 MAX 8和737 MAX 9，而保留了MAX 10的订单。美国航空公司青睐大型窄体飞机的趋势明显，甚至中型737-800和737 MAX 8也已失宠。
这些飞机只是为他们的家庭中的收缩者提供了卓越的经济效益，因为其增加的收入潜力远远超过了增加的燃油消耗。权衡是较短的航程和跑道性能，但只有少数干线车站的条件真正具有挑战性。同时，A320neo和737 MAX系列解决了性能和航程问题。
美国航空公司正在全面升级，改用更大的飞机来执行短途航班。过去，航空公司购买小型飞机的另一个原因是为了调整运力，但美国传统航空公司强烈将票价细分作为核心商业战略。
这减少了运营小型窄体飞机的需求，因为发行不同数量的不同价格的机票可以帮助飞机在飞行速度较慢的日子里填满飞机。联合航空首席执行官斯科特·柯比（Scott Kirby）曾公开评论过这一点。
票价细分和基本经济舱票价意味着他的航空公司不再需要小型窄体飞机来满足需求，从而使美联航能够在更大、更经济的飞机上实现标准化。很明显，美联航在 2016 年订购了 45 737-700 架，又增加了 20 架，然后在同年晚些时候将所有订单转换为 737-800 和 737 MAX 9。
美国航空从空中客车公司订购了 32 架新的 A319-100，同时还购买了一些二手飞机。联合航空将其后来的所有 737-700 订单都改装为更大的型号，同时还购买了少量二手 A319-100。另一方面，达美航空订购了 145 架 A220，同时还采购了 88 717 架。当然，资本成本在其中发挥着巨大作用。

Home Airports Chicago O'Hare Airport (ORD) BREAKING: FAA halts US departures nationwide after air traffic control communications problem

The US Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday, 13 November 2026, at about 15:54 EST (20:54 UTC). The order followed an earlier halt in Chicago after air traffic control communications problems.

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the communications issue affected all US Air Route Traffic Control Centers and that FAA technicians were investigating. The underlying cause has yet to be announced.

The order halted departures from US airports. Aircraft already airborne could still land, and inbound international flights were being handled case by case. This was the first nationwide US departure halt since January 2023.

Latest verified status: The FAA’s initial instruction was to hold departures until further notice. We found no confirmed lifting of the order or nationwide delay and cancellation totals in the available reports.

title_en: Breaking: FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop For All US Flights
title_zh: 突发事件：美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 为所有美国航班在全国范围内停止地面停留
summary: The agency cited communication problems for the halt.
summary_zh: 该机构将暂停的原因归结为沟通问题。
body_en: This article covers a developing story. Continue to check back with us as we will be adding more information as it becomes available.
* Last Updated: 6:00 PM EST November 13, 2026 by Paul Hartley

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a rare nationwide ground stop at all US airports following communication failures affecting "multiple" air traffic control centers on Friday. Citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns, the FAA has suspended all departures until further notice. International arrivals will be handled individually while technicians investigate the disruption.

The exact cause of the ground stop is not yet known, but in a statement obtained by CNBC, the FAA said, "communication issues" impacted air traffic control (ATC) centers. Aviation watchdog JonNYC reported that the halt is not a “9/11 type of event”, which required flights to be forced to land at the closest airport available.
Currently, all airborne aircraft are being allowed to continue flying until further notice. According to FlightAware , more than 6,500 flights are currently halted.

"There has been a temporary telecommunications outage - out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis."

FlightRadar24 is reporting that more than 1,000 flights had already been canceled by 6:00 PM. Cirium data indicates that more than 11,000 flights were still set to depart across the US on Friday after the ground stop was put in place, so cancellations are expected to increase significantly as the evening progresses.
Ground controllers will also face growing difficulty as aircraft continue to land and none depart, putting pressure on already stressed infrastructure and increasignly scarce gate availability.
body_zh: 本文讲述了一个正在发展的故事。请继续与我们联系，因为我们将在可用时添加更多信息。
* 最后更新时间：美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 13 日下午 6:00 作者：Paul Hartley
周五，由于通信故障影响了“多个”空中交通管制中心，美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）下令在美国所有机场进行罕见的全国性地面停留。出于特殊情况和安全考虑，美国联邦航空局已暂停所有航班，直至另行通知。在技​​术人员调查中断情况时，国际抵达航班将被单独处理。
地面停止的确切原因尚不清楚，但在 CNBC 获得的一份声明中，美国联邦航空局表示，“通信问题”影响了空中交通管制（ATC）中心。航空监管机构 JonNYC 报告称，此次停飞并非“9/11 事件”，该事件要求航班被迫降落在最近的机场。
目前，所有机载飞机都被允许继续飞行，直至另行通知。据 FlightAware 称，目前有 6,500 多个航班被暂停。
“发生了暂时的电信中断——出于高度谨慎，所有航班都已停止。每架航班均已清点，国际航班将根据具体情况进行处理。”
FlightRadar24 报告称，截至下午 6:00，已有 1,000 多个航班被取消。 Cirium 数据显示，在地面停靠后，周五仍有超过 11,000 架航班在美国各地起飞，因此随着晚间时间的推移，取消航班预计将大幅增加。
由于飞机继续着陆而没有起飞，地面管制员也将面临越来越大的困难，这给本已紧张的基础设施和日益稀缺的登机口带来了压力。

title_en: How Many Crew Members Does It Take To Fly A KC-135 Stratotanker?
title_zh: 驾驶 KC-135 Stratotanker 需要多少名机组人员？
summary: Its crew arrangement reveals a fascinating story behind this aging US Air Force tanker.
summary_zh: 它的机组人员安排揭示了这架老化的美国空军加油机背后的一个引人入胜的故事。
body_en: Passionate about promoting aviation, the beauty of flight and the science behind it, Antonio is an avid reader of aviation magazines and books, and he loves visiting airshows all over the world, taking photos and writing about airplanes and helicopters as well. He is currently based in Palermo, Sicily.

First flown in 1956, the Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker has spent decades refueling US military aircraft in flight. Despite its age, it remains a major part of the United States Air Force 's tanker fleet, supporting fighters, bombers, and other aircraft on missions around the world. But how many people does it actually take to operate an aircraft responsible for such an important job? The answer raises some interesting questions about how the Stratotanker was designed and how its crew responsibilities have changed over the years.

The KC-135's crew arrangement is not quite as straightforward as it might seem. Its refueling missions require close coordination between the cockpit crew and the operator responsible for transferring fuel, while other missions can bring additional personnel aboard. Its history also raises questions about why it differs from commercial aircraft of the same era and how its crew compares with that of the newer KC-46 Pegasus . Looking at these differences helps explain how the Stratotanker has continued to serve for so many decades.
How Many Crew Members Does A KC-135 Normally Fly With?

For a normal refueling mission, according to the US Air Force's KC-135 fact sheet , the standard crew is three. The KC-135R and KC-135T normally operate with a three-person crew: a pilot, a copilot, and a boom operator. The two pilots occupy the cockpit, while the boom operator works at the rear of the aircraft, controlling the flying boom used to transfer fuel to the receiving aircraft. The National Museum of the US Air Force confirms the same crew number for the KC-135R. The more interesting question is how those three people divide the work.

The workload is substantial. The Air Force fact sheet gives the Stratotanker a maximum takeoff weight of 322,500 pounds (146,285 kg), with up to 200,000 pounds (90,719 kg) of transfer fuel and, depending on configuration, as much as 83,000 pounds (37,648 kg) of cargo. The aircraft carries all of that on a wingspan of 130 feet, 10 inches (39.88 meters), yet the normal crew is still small enough to sit around a kitchen table.

That was not always the case. Early KC-135s carried four people, with a navigator joining the two pilots and boom operator, before advances in navigation and avionics removed that position from the standard crew. The aircraft has nevertheless remained in service for decades. According to Simple Flying , the Air Force still operates roughly 396 Stratotankers across active-duty wings, the Air National Guard and the Air Force Reserve.

More recent Air Force figures cited by the Government Accountability Office put the fleet at 373 aircraft as of early March 2026, before accounting for the losses and damage sustained during Operation Epic Fury against Iran. The Congressional Research Service later listed seven KC-135s as lost or damaged during the conflict. With hundreds of Stratotankers still in the inventory and the basic crew arrangement remaining central to their operation, the obvious next question is what each crew member is actually responsible for.

The three-person crew arrangement makes more sense once the KC-135's refueling system comes into view. Aerial refueling requires two aircraft to maintain close formation while a rigid boom connects them in flight. The Air Force lists the KC-135's maximum speed at 530 miles per hour (853 km/h) at 30,000 feet (9,144 meters), although fuel transfer takes place at speeds appropriate to the aircraft involved. The receiving jet moves into position below and behind the tanker, the boom extends, and the final connection is made from the rear of the Stratotanker.

Each crew member has a specific responsibility. The pilot flies the tanker and maintains a stable flight path, while the copilot shares flying duties, handles communications and checklists, and monitors aircraft systems. At the back, the boom operator, an enlisted airman, controls the boom and guides its nozzle into the receiving aircraft. The National Museum of the US Air Force explains that the operator uses small wing-like control surfaces called ruddervators to steer the boom into position. Working from a prone position and looking through a window, the operator effectively flies the boom itself. The system can transfer nearly all the KC-135's usable fuel, while a drogue attachment can be fitted to support aircraft equipped with refueling probes. The arrangement has proved capable of some extraordinary missions.

The museum's KC-135R earned the Mackay Trophy for a sortie flown on May 31, 1967, after a Navy pilot was shot down in Southeast Asia and a rescue operation ran into fuel difficulties. Two US Navy Douglas KA-3 Skywarriors kept a pair of Vought F-8 Crusaders airborne, but both the tankers and the fighters were running low on fuel. The KC-135 crew began refueling the KA-3s while continuing to pass fuel to the F-8s. In effect, one tanker was refueling another tanker that was simultaneously refueling a fighter. The KC-135 subsequently provided additional fuel to two McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom fighters on its way to an alternative landing base.

Interestingly, although the KC-135 could operate with a basic crew of three, the aircraft involved in this award-winning mission carried four. Its crew consisted of Major John H. Casteel, aircraft commander; Captain Richard L. Trail, copilot; Captain Dean L. Hoar, navigator; and Master Sergeant Nathan C. Campbell, boom operator. This historical example illustrates the distinction between the aircraft's earlier four-person arrangement and its modern standard crew. The additional crew member was a navigator, not a flight engineer.

The navigator's presence on earlier KC-135 missions helps explain how the tanker's crew evolved over time, but it also highlights a more fundamental difference between the aircraft and its civilian contemporaries: the absence of a dedicated flight engineer. The tanker was developed alongside the Boeing 707, and many airliners of the period used a third cockpit crewmember to monitor engines and systems. Yet Air Force records for the KC-135 identify pilots, a boom operator and, on earlier versions, a navigator.
body_zh: 安东尼奥热衷于推广航空、飞行之美及其背后的科学，是航空杂志和书籍的狂热读者，他喜欢参观世界各地的航展，也喜欢拍摄有关飞机和直升机的照片和撰写有关飞机和直升机的文章。他目前居住在西西里岛巴勒莫。
波音 KC-135 Stratotanker 于 1956 年首飞，数十年来一直在为飞行中的美国军用飞机加油。尽管年代久远，它仍然是美国空军加油机机队的主要​​组成部分，为在世界各地执行任务的战斗机、轰炸机和其他飞机提供支持。但实际上需要多少人来操作负责如此重要工作的飞机呢？这个答案提出了一些有趣的问题，涉及平流层油轮的设计方式以及多年来其船员职责如何变化。
KC-135 的机组人员安排并不像看起来那么简单。其加油任务需要驾驶舱机组人员和负责传输燃料的操作员之间的密切协调，而其他任务则可以携带更多人员。它的历史也引发了人们的疑问：为什么它与同时代的商用飞机不同，以及它的机组人员与较新的 KC-46 Pegasus 的机组人员相比如何。了解这些差异有助于解释同温层油轮如何持续服役数十年。
KC-135 通常搭载多少名机组人员？
根据美国空军的KC-135情况说明书，对于正常的加油任务，标准机组人员为三人。 KC-135R 和 KC-135T 通常由三人机组人员操作：一名飞行员、一名副驾驶和一名动臂操作员。两名飞行员占据驾驶舱，而吊杆操作员在飞机后部工作，控制用于将燃油传输到接收飞机的飞行吊杆。美国空军国家博物馆确认 KC-135R 的机组人员编号相同。更有趣的问题是这三个人如何分工。
工作量很大。空军资料表显示，Stratotanker 的最大起飞重量为 322,500 磅（146,285 公斤），可装载高达 200,000 磅（90,719 公斤）的燃油，根据配置，最多可装载 83,000 磅（37,648 公斤）的货物。这架飞机在 130 英尺 10 英寸（39.88 米）的翼展上承载了所有这些，但普通机组人员仍然小到可以坐在厨房的桌子旁。
情况并非总是如此。早期的 KC-135 飞机可搭载 4 人，其中一名导航员与两名飞行员和动臂操作员一起，后来导航和航空电子设备的进步从标准机组人员中取消了这一职位。尽管如此，这架飞机仍然服役了几十年。据 Simple Flying 报道，空军现役联队、空军国民警卫队和空军预备役部队中仍有大约 396 架同温层加油机。
美国政府问责办公室引用的最新空军数据显示，截至 2026 年 3 月上旬，空军机队拥有 373 架飞机，这还不包括针对伊朗的史诗愤怒行动期间遭受的损失和损害。国会研究服务处后来列出了 7 架 KC-135 在冲突期间丢失或损坏的情况。由于库存中仍有数百艘同温层油轮，而且基本的船员安排仍然是其运作的核心，下一个明显的问题是每个船员实际上负责什么。
一旦看到 KC-135 的加油系统，三人机组人员的安排就更有意义了。空中加油需要两架飞机保持紧密队形，同时用刚性吊杆在飞行中将它们连接起来。空军列出的 KC-135 在 30,000 英尺（9,144 米）高度的最大速度为 530 英里/小时（853 公里/小时），尽管燃料传输的速度适合所涉及的飞机。接收喷射器移动到油轮下方和后方的位置，吊杆伸出，最后的连接是从平流层油轮的后部进行的。

每个船员都有特定的责任。飞行员驾驶加油机并保持稳定的飞行路线，而副驾驶则分担飞行职责，处理通信和检查表，并监控飞机系统。在后面，吊杆操作员（一名现役飞行员）控制吊杆并将其喷嘴引导到接收飞机中。美国空军国家博物馆解释说，操作员使用称为方向舵的小型机翼状控制面来将吊杆引导到位。操作员俯卧工作并透过窗户观察，可以有效地驾驶吊杆本身。该系统可以传输几乎所有 KC-135 的可用燃料，同时可以安装锥套附件来支持配备加油探头的飞机。事实证明，这种安排能够完成一些非凡的任务。

1967 年 5 月 31 日，一名海军飞行员在东南亚被击落，救援行动遇到燃料困难，博物馆的 KC-135R 因一次飞行而获得了麦凯奖。两架美国海军道格拉斯 KA-3 空中战士让两架沃特 F-8 十字军战斗机在空中飞行，但加油机和战斗机的燃油都已不足。 KC-135 机组人员开始为 KA-3 加油，同时继续向 F-8 输送燃油。实际上，一架加油机正在为另一架加油机加油，而另一架加油机同时也在为一架战斗机加油。 KC-135 随后为两架飞往替代着陆基地的麦道 F-4 幻影战斗机提供了额外的燃料。

有趣的是，虽然 KC-135 的基本机组人员为 3 人，但参与此次获奖任务的飞机却搭载了 4 名机组人员。其机组人员包括飞机指挥官约翰·H·卡斯蒂尔少校；理查德·L·特雷尔 (Richard L. Trail) 机长，副驾驶； Dean L. Hoar 船长，航海家；还有军士长内森·C·坎贝尔（Nathan C. Campbell），动臂操作员。这个历史例子说明了飞机早期的四人安排和现代标准机组人员之间的区别。额外的机组人员是一名领航员，而不是飞行工程师。
导航员在早期 KC-135 任务中的出现有助于解释加油机机组人员如何随着时间的推移而发展，但它也凸显了该飞机与同时代民用飞机之间更根本的区别：缺乏专门的飞行工程师。该加油机是与波音 707 一起开发的，当时的许多客机都使用第三名驾驶舱机组人员来监控发动机和系统。然而，KC-135 的空军记录显示了飞行员、吊杆操作员以及早期版本的导航员。

title_en: How To Redeem World Of Hyatt Points For Best Value, Maximize Award Chart
title_zh: 如何兑换凯悦天地积分以获得最佳价值、最大化奖励图表
summary: World of Hyatt is my favorite hotel loyalty program. Here's how the award charts work, what points are worth, and how I consistently redeem for over two cents each.
summary_zh: 凯悦天地是我最喜欢的酒店忠诚度计划。以下是奖励图表的运作方式、积分的价值以及我如何持续兑换超过 t
body_en: I write a lot about the value of hotel loyalty programs , and in this post, I’d like to talk about World of Hyatt. What are the best ways to redeem World of Hyatt points, how many points do you need for a free night redemption, how does the award chart work, etc.?
World of Hyatt award chart & redemptions explained

Let’s start by talking about the basics of redeeming World of Hyatt points — how much should you expect to pay for free nights, are there blackout dates, how much are World of Hyatt points worth, etc.?
My World of Hyatt points valuation of 1.4 cents

Based on my latest miles & points valuations , I consider World of Hyatt points to be worth 1.4 cents each. There’s no science to that, but rather I think that’s a fair, conservative valuation for what the points are worth. In other words, I won’t redeem points for a hotel stay with Hyatt unless I’m getting well over 1.4 cents of value per point (and that has to factor in the points I’m forgoing by redeeming rather than paying cash, etc.).
It’s important to come up with a points valuation for yourself (it can be different than mine), so that you can decide whether to pay cash or redeem points for a hotel stay.
I have lowered this valuation a little recently, in light of the World of Hyatt award chart devaluation we’ve seen, where Hyatt has gone from three tiers of pricing within each category to five.
World of Hyatt has no blackout dates , which is to say that if a standard room is available for sale with cash, it can also be booked with points.

Now, the important thing to keep in mind is that some hotels have a very small pool of “standard” rooms, and a vast majority of rooms at a hotel may be considered “premium.” If a hotel has 150 rooms, it’s possible that only 10 rooms are considered “standard,” so that’s the major issue you’ll run into when redeeming points at some properties.

Unfortunately in the hotel industry overall, we’ve seen a reduction in the number of standard rooms at many properties that are popular for redemptions, which is essentially a way for hotels to create indirect capacity controls.
Keep in mind that Hyatt has a great points availability calendar , which at least makes it easy to find the nights that are available with points, for those properties that are challenging.

Hopefully this isn’t an issue anyone runs into, but just keep in mind the World of Hyatt points expiration policy . World of Hyatt points expire after 24 months of inactivity. Any points earning or redemption activity resets the expiration of your points by a further 24 months.
Redeem World of Hyatt points for free night awards

Unlike Hilton Honors, IHG One Rewards, and Marriott Bonvoy, World of Hyatt continues to publish award charts for award redemptions (the exception is Mr & Mrs Smith properties, which I’ll talk more about in a bit).

The catch is that at this point, World of Hyatt has five tiers of award pricing for standard room redemptions — Lowest, Low, Moderate, Upper, and Top — and the variance within each category is huge. So while I appreciate that there’s not technically dynamic pricing, when a Category 1 hotel can cost 3,000 or 9,000 points, and a Category 8 hotel can cost 35,000 or 75,000 points, you’re not exactly getting a lot of assurance.

The standard award chart applies at a vast majority of properties globally, including most Hyatt branded properties. There are eight categories of hotels, and 40 different pricing tiers, given the five pricing bands within each tier. Pricing ranges from 3,000 points for a Category 1 property during the “Lowest” period, and 75,000 points for a Category 8 property during the “Top” period.

Next, World of Hyatt has an all-inclusive award chart, which applies to an ever-growing number of properties across Hyatt’s all-inclusive brands. Hotels fall into one of six categories, with the similar five bands of pricing, all based on double occupancy. Pricing ranges from 12,000 points for a Category A property during the “Lowest” period, to 85,000 points for a Category F property during the “Top” period.

Lastly, World of Hyatt has an award chart for Miraval properties , which are Hyatt’s super-luxurious wellness resorts. Pricing varies based on single or double occupancy, and then there’s also the five bands of pricing.
body_zh: 我写了很多关于酒店忠诚度计划价值的文章，在这篇文章中，我想谈谈凯悦天地。兑换凯悦天地积分的最佳方式是什么、兑换免费住宿需要多少积分、奖励表如何运作等？
凯悦天地奖励表和兑换说明
让我们首先讨论一下兑换凯悦天地积分的基础知识 - 您应该为免费住宿支付多少钱、是否有限制日期、凯悦天地积分值多少钱等？
我的凯悦世界积分估值为 1.4 美分
根据我最新的里程和积分估值，我认为凯悦天地积分每个价值 1.4 美分。这没有科学依据，但我认为这是对积分价值的公平、保守的评估。换句话说，我不会用积分兑换凯悦酒店住宿，除非我每积分获得的价值远远超过 1.4 美分（这必须考虑到我通过兑换而不是支付现金等方式放弃的积分）。
为自己制定一个积分估值（可能与我的不同）很重要，这样您就可以决定是否支付现金或兑换积分来入住酒店。
鉴于我们所看到的凯悦天地奖励图表贬值，我最近稍微降低了这一估值，其中凯悦已将每个类别的定价从三级调整为五级。
凯悦天地没有限制日期，也就是说，如果标准间可以用现金出售，也可以用积分预订。
现在，要记住的重要一点是，一些酒店的“标准”客房数量非常少，而酒店的绝大多数房间可能被视为“高级”客房。如果一家酒店有 150 间客房，则可能只有 10 间客房被视为“标准”房间，因此这是您在某些酒店兑换积分时会遇到的主要问题。
不幸的是，在整个酒店行业，我们发现许多受欢迎的酒店的标准间数量减少了，这本质上是酒店建立间接容量控制的一种方式。
请记住，凯悦酒店有一个很棒的积分可用日历，这至少可以让您轻松找到可以使用积分的住宿，对于那些具有挑战性的酒店。
希望这不是任何人都会遇到的问题，但请记住凯悦天地积分过期政策。凯悦天地积分在 24 个月不活动后过期。任何积分赚取或兑换活动都会将您的积分有效期再重置 24 个月。
使用凯悦天地积分兑换免费住宿奖励
与希尔顿荣誉客会、洲际酒店集团 One Rewards 和万豪旅享家不同，凯悦天地继续发布奖励兑换的奖励图表（史密斯夫妇酒店除外，我稍后会详细讨论）。
问题是，目前凯悦天地为标准客房兑换提供了五个等级的奖励定价——最低、低、中等、较高和顶级——而且每个类别之间的差异很大。因此，虽然我很欣赏技术上不存在动态定价，但当 1 类酒店的费用为 3,000 或 9,000 积分，而 8 类酒店的费用为 35,000 或 75,000 积分时，您并没有得到太多的保证。
标准奖励表适用于全球绝大多数酒店，包括大多数凯悦品牌酒店。酒店有 8 个类别和 40 个不同的定价等级，每个等级有 5 个定价区间。在“最低”期间，第 1 类酒店的定价范围为 3,000 点，在“最高”期间，第 8 类酒店的定价范围为 75,000 点。
其次，凯悦天地有一个全包奖励表，适用于凯悦全包品牌中越来越多的酒店。酒店分为六类之一，具有类似的五个定价等级，全部基于双人入住。定价范围从“最低”期间 A 类房产的 12,000 点到“最高”期间 F 类房产的 85,000 点不等。
最后，凯悦天地有 Miraval 物业的奖励表，这些物业是凯悦旗下的超豪华健康度假村。定价根据单人或双人入住而有所不同，还有五个定价区间。

body_en: James lives and breathes route development. Educated in Air Transport Management at Loughborough University and Cranfield University, James has a PhD in Airline Strategy and Economics. James was Market Opportunity Analyst at London Luton Airport and Chief Analyst at anna.aero. He taught airline strategy and economics to undergraduate and postgraduate students for five years and has worked closely with multiple carriers on route and market intelligence projects. He is based near London, UK.

Allegiant Air has flown to Myrtle Beach since 2009. Cirium Diio data shows that it was the ultra-low-cost carrier's third destination in South Carolina. It came after Columbia, the capital, and Greenville/Spartanburg, both first served 20 years ago. All flights to Columbia have now ended .

Myrtle Beach is renowned for being a family-friendly beach destination. It has tens of miles of white sand, along with being the so-called golf capital of the world. It is not a surprise that it had held much appeal for Allegiant for so long, at least until now, just as it is increasingly doing for Breeze .

Comparing the airline's schedule in 2026 with what is planned for 2027 shows that all of these routes are no longer scheduled. They were cross-referenced with what is listed on Allegiant's website, and all the routes were removed. The 13 markets are in nine states. While only two of the removed destinations are now served by another carrier, all nine states will still have flights, whether by Allegiant or a different operator.

US Department of Transportation data shows that Allegiant flew between Myrtle Beach and Atlantic City between March and August 2026. It had inherited the route from the now-defunct Spirit Airlines, which had served it for 29 years until early 2026. Allegiant transported 11,453 passengers and filled 80.5% of seats. While fare information is unavailable, the extremely short period shows that the route performed very poorly. Despite this, Breeze is keen, as flights started in October.
Allegiant Now Has Nine Routes From Myrtle Beach

The cuts outlined above are only one part of Allegiant's story at Myrtle Beach. The ultra-low-cost carrier's booking engine currently extends to mid-May 2027. Between January and then, the airline plans to fly to nine places from Myrtle Beach: Akron/Canton, Albany, Allentown, Cincinnati, Columbus Rickenbacker, Harrisburg, Pittsburgh, Stewart, and Syracuse.

217 departures will be available on those nine routes through May 2027, down by 31% compared to January to May 2026. Seven of the markets will have fewer flights than they did, none more so than Akron/Canton, which Allegiant partly serves because Cleveland is only around an hour away. Departures in the first five months are down from 26 to just eight. In 2026, Allegiant served the market from March. Now it'll do so from May.
All Nine Affected States Will Still Have Myrtle Beach Flights

Most of the nine states will, of course, have flights to other places, rather than those dropped by Allegiant. Myrtle Beach will have flights to Illinois with American (Chicago O'Hare), Southwest (Chicago Midway), and United (O'Hare), while Indiana will be served by Southwest (Indianapolis).

Then there's Kentucky , with Allegiant flying to Cincinnati (the airport is in Kentucky, but the city is in Ohio), Maryland is linked with Southwest (Baltimore), Michigan's in the hands of Delta (Detroit), and New Jersey's served by Breeze (Atlantic City) and United (Newark).

New York has many routes from Allegiant (Albany, Stewart, Syracuse), American (LaGuardia), Breeze (Albany, Buffalo, Islip, Rochester, Stewart, Syracuse, Westchester), and Delta (LaGuardia). title_en: Final Authority: The Pilot-Ceding Rule Every Air Traffic Controller Is Taught At Birth
title_zh: 最终权力：每个空中交通管制员出生时就被教导的飞行员让出规则
summary: From dangerous thunderstorms to fatal midair collisions, aviation history reveals why pilots sometimes must reject air traffic control instructions.
summary_zh: 从危险的雷暴到致命的空中相撞，航空历史揭示了为什么飞行员有时必须拒绝空中交通管制指令。
body_en: Paul has had a career of 25+ years focused on the international technology sector, which has taken him to over 100 countries. Along the way, he developed a deep love for aviation, with a travel bucket list measured by aircraft types flown rather than destinations reached. Now he brings that avgeek passion, along with the journalism experience he accumulated early in his career, to write insightful pieces for Simple Flying.

On September 3, a JetBlue Airways captain climbing out of Fort Lauderdale faced an extraordinary choice: follow ATC instructions toward what appeared to be a severe thunderstorm, or take matters into his own hands. When the controller refused his requested alternative heading, citing conflicting traffic, the captain declared an emergency and began turning away.

The incident was notable enough that it was reported by View From The Wing at the time, which concluded that "declaring an emergency is no longer asking for permission: it is telling air traffic control what they are doing." It would also resonate just two months later when a Learjet 60 with nine people on board crashed after encountering severe turbulence in the same South Florida airspace.

It subsequently emerged that the ill-fated aircraft had a history of miscommunicating severe weather with ATC. The JetBlue confrontation demonstrated a fundamental principle of commercial aviation: although pilots ordinarily follow ATC clearances, ultimate operational responsibility belongs to the aircraft's captain.

Federal regulations recognize circumstances in which pilots may override instructions, sometimes without advance permission. From the Miracle on the Hudson to a deadly collision over Germany , aviation history reveals why that authority exists, and what can happen when pilots do not exercise it.
The JetBlue Captain Who Refused To Fly Into A Thunderstorm

JetBlue flight B61971, operated by an Airbus A320 with the registration N715JB, departed Fort Lauderdale for Austin (AUS) 76 minutes late. During its climb, ATC assigned a 270-degree heading, but the crew believed that course would take them into severe weather. The pilots requested 250 or 240 degrees instead. The controller refused, explaining that other aircraft occupied the requested airspace and that her display showed a gap in the precipitation.

JetBlue's captain challenged that assessment, asking whether the controller intended to send them through a severe thunderstorm. The controller responded that she saw only " light precipitation " on the designated heading, to which the pilot responded
"Not from the air, ma'am. So we declare an emergency, making a left turn heading two-six-zero for severe weather avoidance.”

ATC acknowledged the emergency, and the pilot subsequently reported new headings as the aircraft turned through 240 and 230 degrees. The pilot later explained to the controller that the severe weather on the previous heading was why they had declared an emergency, saying that " you do what you gotta do, we gotta do what we gotta do here ."
The Federal Rule That Gives Pilots The Final Say

The authority exercised by JetBlue's captain originates in 14 CFR 91.3 . It establishes the pilot in command's ultimate responsibility and permits necessary deviations from Part 91 rules during emergencies requiring immediate action. Meanwhile, 14 CFR 91.123 provides explicit exceptions to ATC-clearance compliance, and 121.557 grants airline captains emergency operational authority.

These provisions do not permit arbitrary disregard of instructions. Controllers have substantial responsibilities of their own. They must maintain separation between aircraft, even when crews request weather deviations. FAA Order JO 7110.65 instructs controllers who cannot approve a requested deviation because of traffic to seek another solution that accommodates weather avoidance.
Emergencies and TCAS advisories permit deviations
ATC seeks weather-safe alternatives while separating traffic

That helps explain the JetBlue controller's concerns: approving the crew's preferred heading without resolving conflicting traffic could have introduced another danger. These principles extend into airline procedures. Airline Flight Operations Manuals will document the captain's responsibility for safe operations and command over the crew​​​​​​.

Some manuals explicitly direct captains to declare emergencies in the event of severe weather that cannot otherwise be avoided. The FAA's foundational statement behind this is unequivocal, and concludes that " the pilot in command of an aircraft is directly responsible for, and is the final authority as to, the operation of that aircraft ."
Is Declaring An Emergency Necessary To Override ATC?
Credit: Wirestock Creators | Shutterstock, Simple Flying

Most disagreements never reach the emergency stage. Pilots typically request amended headings, routes, or altitudes, explaining why an assigned clearance is unsuitable. The word " unable " is used to communicate that an instruction cannot safely be accepted. The FAA explicitly encourages pilots to challenge instructions that would jeopardize safety.
body_zh: Paul 拥有超过 25 年的职业生涯，专注于国际技术领域，足迹遍布 100 多个国家。一路走来，他对航空产生了深深的热爱，他的旅行愿望清单是根据飞行的飞机类型而不是到达的目的地来衡量的。现在，他带着这种平均极客的热情，以及他在职业生涯早期积累的新闻经验，为《简单飞行》撰写了富有洞察力的文章。
9 月 3 日，捷蓝航空的一名机长从劳德代尔堡爬出，面临着一个非同寻常的选择：遵循 ATC 的指示应对看似严重的雷暴天气，还是亲自处理此事。当管制员以交通冲突为由拒绝他请求的替代航向时，机长宣布紧急情况并开始掉头离开。
这一事件非常引人注目，当时《View From The Wing》对此进行了报道，其结论是“宣布紧急状态不再是征求许可：而是告诉空中交通管制人员他们在做什么。”仅仅两个月后，一架载有 9 人的里尔 60 型飞机在南佛罗里达州同一空域遭遇严重湍流后坠毁，这也引发了共鸣。
随后发现，这架命运多舛的飞机曾与空中交通管制部门错误传达恶劣天气的历史。捷蓝航空的对抗展示了商业航空的一个基本原则：尽管飞行员通常遵守空中交通管制许可，但最终的运营责任属于飞机的机长。
联邦法规承认飞行员可以推翻指令的情况，有时未经事先许可。从哈德逊河奇迹到德国上空的致命碰撞，航空史揭示了这种权力存在的原因，以及如果飞行员不行使这种权力会发生什么。
拒绝飞入雷暴的捷蓝航空机长
捷蓝航空 B61971 航班由注册号为 N715JB 的空客 A320 运营，从劳德代尔堡出发飞往奥斯汀（澳大利亚），晚点 76 分钟。在爬升过程中，ATC 指定了 270 度的航向，但机组人员认为这个航向会让他们陷入恶劣的天气。飞行员要求改为 250 或 240 度。管制员拒绝了，并解释说其他飞机占据了所请求的空域，并且她的显示器显示降水量有差距。
捷蓝航空的机长对这一评估提出质疑，询问管制员是否打算让他们经历一场严重的雷暴。管制员回应说，她在指定航向上只看到“轻微降水”，飞行员对此回应
“不是从空中飞来的，女士。所以我们宣布进入紧急状态，向二六零的方向左转，以避免恶劣天气。”
ATC 承认了紧急情况，飞行员随后报告了飞机转向 240 度和 230 度时的新航向。飞行员后来向管制员解释说，前一个航向的恶劣天气是他们宣布紧急状态的原因，他说：“你做你必须做的事，我们必须做我们在这里必须做的事。”
赋予飞行员最终决定权的联邦规则
捷蓝航空机长行使的权力源自 14 CFR 91.3。它规定了机长的最终责任，并允许在需要立即采取行动的紧急情况下对第 91 部分规则进行必要的偏离。同时，14 CFR 91.123 规定了 ATC 许可合规性的明确例外情况，121.557 则授予航空公司机长紧急操作权限。
这些规定不允许任意无视指示。控制者本身负有重大责任。即使机组人员要求天气偏差，他们也必须保持飞机之间的距离。 FAA 命令 JO 7110.65 指示由于交通原因而无法批准偏离请求的管制员寻求另一种适应天气规避的解决方案。
紧急情况和 TCAS 建议允许偏差
空中交通管制在隔离交通的同时寻求天气安全的替代方案
这有助于解释捷蓝航空管制员的担忧：在不解决交通冲突的情况下批准机组人员的首选航向可能会带来另一种危险。这些原则延伸到航空公司的程序中。航空公司飞行操作手册将记录机长对安全操作和对机组人员的指挥的责任​​​​​​。
一些手册明确指示船长在发生无法避免的恶劣天气时宣布紧急情况。美国联邦航空局对此的基本声明是明确的，并得出结论：“驾驶飞机的飞行员直接负责该飞机的操作，并且是该飞机操作的最终权力。”
是否需要宣布紧急情况才能推翻 ATC？
图片来源：Wirestock Creators | Shutterstock，简单飞行
大多数分歧从未达到紧急阶段。飞行员通常会要求修改航向、航线或高度，并解释为什么指定的许可不合适。 “无法”一词用于表示无法安全地接受指令。美国联邦航空局明确鼓励飞行员挑战可能危及安全的指令。

JetBlue has removed a considerable 35 routes from its network, of which 22 are domestic and 13 are international. They all operated at some point in the first ten months of 2026 , but no flights are scheduled in the future.

In winter 2026/2027, JetBlue's schedule submission to Cirium Diio data shows an average of 919 daily departures (double for total movements). Compared to the prior winter, 7% more activity is scheduled. By far the main winner is Fort Lauderdale , with departures up by a staggering 58%, influenced by the end of Spirit. In contrast, Newark flights are down by 32%.

Analyzing the evolving carrier's entire network identified that the following markets no longer exist. The examined period only includes January to October 2026, with any routes that will end in November 2026 or thereafter not mentioned. They'll be explored separately another time.
New York JFK to Ponce (in the US territory of Puerto Rico)

Hartford to Tampa, Manchester to Orlando, Newark to Tampa
Boston to Daytona Beach, New York JFK to Daytona Beach, New York JFK to Vero Beach
Newark to Los Angeles, New York JFK to Chicago O'Hare , New York JFK to Nashville

Despite the big overall growth at Fort Lauderdale, the South Florida airport has seen the most eliminated domestic routes. However, this is primarily because most only operated very briefly for spring break. The cuts included Reno, from which no flights to Fort Lauderdale (or Florida generally) previously existed. Given the US Department of Transportation (DOT) shows a load factor of 60.1%, it is hardly surprising that JetBlue isn't returning.
